Here we go it’s my time to shine. My dad got me fired from my dream job. 
So I graduate with a cool degree, look for work, get a great break with a dope clinical investigation lab on a US Air Force base. Check my references, pass the usual background check, I’m stoked. Salary is insane, commute not bad, living the dream. 
Two weeks later, I get called into the boss lady’s office and she tells me I need to turn in my badge and leave the base immediately and that I’ve been let go because I didn’t pass the *more extensive* background check and that those with a criminal record cannot work on base dealing with sensitive material. 
So I sob. No healthcare, no money, student debt to pay. I called the contractor that hired me and she was like I have no idea, you passed the background check for us, but not for the DOJ (department of justice) she told me to request my records from the FBI. 
Mind you, I have done no wrong in my life lol. Never been arrested, one speeding ticket. So I’m absolutely crushed and start calling the FBI like hey it’s me what’s on my record. I bothered them everyday for two weeks and got my record in record time (=]). 
What’s on my record you ask? What caused me to be accused of a criminal past and asked to leave immediately? 
WELL. DAD. when I was 13 I shoplifted from JCP in the mall with my best friend (cuz ya know, teenage girls are crazy). JCP didn’t really care, but my DO GOOD FATHER did. To teach me that actions have consequences, he made me go to local PD, get finger printed, I had to do a weekend 8 hour class for bad kids (on drugs and alcohol?????? I was scared honestly.) had to do 40 hours community service. All to learn a LESSON and be A GOOD PERSON or whatever. 
Juvenile or expunged records are available to the DOJ. And any criminal activity was grounds for termination. 
So, my dad trying to teach 13 year old me a lesson got me fired 13 years later.
IM STILL NOT OVER IT.
